subject: Biology

stem: Seeds from two shrub populations were germinated after different heat treatments. Group A came from frequently burned sites and group B from rarely burned sites.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Identify the temperature giving the largest difference in germination.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Calculate the percentage-point difference at 80 degrees C.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Compare responses of the two groups.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain why fluctuating field temperatures should be recorded.

parts.label: e
parts.html: Predict which group will be favoured if fires become more frequent, with reasons.

parts.label: f
parts.html: Suggest two controls for a repeat experiment.

questions.title: Thermal tolerance after fire

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: 80 degrees C.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: 72 - 38 = 34 percentage points.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Both peak at moderate heat; A exceeds B at 60-100 degrees C; germination falls at 120 degrees C in both, with a steeper fall in B.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Laboratory constant temperatures may not represent exposure duration/peaks; field data improve ecological validity and link germination to actual conditions.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: Group A; it has higher germination after strong heating; survivors reproduce after fires; alleles for heat-tolerant germination increase by natural selection.

solparts.label: f
solparts.html: Any two of seed age, hydration, heating duration, sample size, light, germination time and growth medium.

stem: Proteins are assembled from amino acids on ribosomes.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Distinguish essential from non-essential amino acids in humans.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State the roles of mRNA and tRNA in translation.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Outline peptide-bond formation.

questions.title: Amino acids and translation

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized in sufficient amounts and must be obtained in the diet; non-essential amino acids can be synthesized.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: mRNA carries codons copied from DNA; tRNA carries a specific amino acid and has an anticodon complementary to an mRNA codon.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: A condensation reaction joins the amino and carboxyl groups; water is released and a covalent peptide bond forms.

stem: A filamentous fungus has multinucleate hyphae containing mitochondria and vacuoles.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Deduce that the fungus is eukaryotic.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State one component of a fungal cell wall.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain the term aseptate hypha.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain two properties of water important in the cytoplasm.

questions.title: Fungal cell organization

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: It contains nuclei and membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria/vacuoles.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Chitin / glucans / glycoproteins.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: The hypha is not divided into separate cells by cross-walls and contains continuous cytoplasm with many nuclei.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Polarity makes water a solvent for ions/polar molecules; hydrogen bonding gives high specific heat capacity; water participates in hydrolysis/condensation reactions. Any two well explained.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Explain why active transport requires ATP.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State where most ATP is produced during aerobic respiration.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Outline how ATP is regenerated.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Particles move against a concentration/electrochemical gradient; ATP hydrolysis changes the shape of a carrier/pump and supplies energy.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Mitochondria / inner mitochondrial membrane by oxidative phosphorylation.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: ADP combines with inorganic phosphate by phosphorylation; energy from respiration or light drives the endergonic reaction.

stem: A motor neuron communicates with a muscle fibre across a synaptic cleft.
Answer 1 of the following questions. One additional construction mark is available for each response.

parts.label: a
parts.html: State the type of substance stored in synaptic vesicles.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State two differences between pre- and postsynaptic membranes.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain why the cleft is narrow.

questions.title: Chemical synapses

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: A neurotransmitter, for example acetylcholine.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Presynaptic membrane has vesicles and voltage-gated Ca2+ channels; postsynaptic membrane has neurotransmitter receptors/ligand-gated ion channels.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Short diffusion distance permits rapid neurotransmitter signalling.

stem: Homeostatic systems keep internal conditions within limits.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Compare positive and negative feedback, using one example of each.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Explain regulation of blood glucose after a carbohydrate-rich meal.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain how ventilation contributes to blood pH regulation.

questions.title: Feedback and blood variables

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Negative feedback reverses deviation from a set point, for example blood glucose or temperature; positive feedback amplifies change, for example oxytocin during labour or clotting, until an endpoint.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Beta cells detect high glucose and release insulin; insulin binds target-cell receptors; increases glucose uptake and glycogenesis in liver/muscle; reduces blood glucose; secretion falls by negative feedback. Include glucagon as the opposing response when glucose is low.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: CO2 combines with water to form carbonic acid; high CO2 lowers pH; chemoreceptors detect change; respiratory centre increases ventilation; more CO2 is exhaled and pH moves back towards normal.

solution: Construction [1] Award for a coherent, logically ordered response using appropriate biological terminology.

stem: Unrelated organisms can evolve similar solutions to the same environmental challenge.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Explain how analogous structures evolve.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Describe adaptations of plants to dry habitats.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain how natural selection can produce piercing mouthparts in sap-feeding insects.

questions.title: Convergent evolution in dry habitats

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Unrelated populations show heritable variation; similar selection pressures favour similar functions; allele frequencies change independently; structures have similar functions but different evolutionary origins.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Any six developed points: reduced leaves/spines; thick waxy cuticle; sunken/fewer stomata; CAM with stomata open at night; succulent water storage; extensive/deep roots; leaf hairs/rolled leaves.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Variation arises by mutation/recombination; individuals with effective piercing/feeding obtain more resources; survive and reproduce more; advantageous alleles are inherited; frequency rises over generations.
